chunks.section_title: Procedure on Pre-Enrollment Student's Health Assessment (PRE-SHA)
chunks.process_name: Procedure on Pre-Enrollment Student's Health Assessment (PRE-SHA)
chunks.content: Step 1: Submission of Medical Requirements. Applicant submits all medical requirements: Student Health Record, Health Declaration Form, Diagnostic Laboratory Test Results and other pertinent medical records, e.g. PWD ID, previous medical records if applicable. Medical Staff receives, collects, and checks all documents. Step 2: Physical Health Assessment. Applicant consents to undergo physical examination and health assessment. Medical Officer conducts medical evaluation and physical examination. Step 3: Issuance of Medical Clearance / Medical Advise. Medical Officer issues Medical Clearance to applicants who are physically fit to enroll. Otherwise, medical advice or referral is given for further compliance. Step 4: Health Services Satisfaction Survey. Nurse sends the HSSS QR Code thru email. After receiving Medical Clearance, applicant answers the Health Services Satisfaction Survey (HSSS) posted or emailed to them.  Contacts: Email: tupt.clinic@tup.edu.ph, Facebook: TUP-Taguig Clinic, Messenger: TUP-Taguig Clinic

chunks.section_title: Procedure for Dental Treatment
chunks.content: Step 1: Schedule Appointment. Patient visits the Campus Dental Clinic to book a schedule for dental treatment. Dental aide logs patient’s preferred schedule. Dental aide informs the Dentist of the scheduled dental treatment. Step 2: Dental Treatment. Patient visits Campus Dental Clinic on the day of the scheduled appointment. Dental Aide assists the patient and informs the Dentist of the scheduled treatment. The Dentist performs oral examination to the patient to determine the specific treatment to be done. Dentist performs dental treatment to the patient. Step 3: Post Treatment. Dentist gives post treatment instructions, prescription, and medication to the patient. Patient receives post treatment instructions, prescription, and medication. Step 4: Client Feedback. Dental aide gives the Client Satisfaction Measurement Survey via hard copy or Google Form. Patient signs the logbook after the dental care consultation and answers the Client Satisfaction Measurement Survey Form.

chunks.section_title: Procedure for Dental Emergency Treatment
chunks.content: Step 1: Informs Dental Aide of Chief Complaint. Patient informs the dental aide of their chief complaint. Dental Aide asks for patient’s information and locates its dental record. Dental Aide informs the dentist about the patient’s chief complaint and provides the dental record of the patient. Step 2: Dental Treatment. Patient informs the Dentist of his/her chief complaint and answers questions asked by the dentist. The Dentist performs oral treatment, gives advice to patient, provides referral if oral x-ray is needed, and prescribes medicine. Patient proceeds to see the dental aide after the treatment. Step 3: Post Treatment. Patient receives post treatment instructions, prescription, proceeds to the dental aide, and presents the prescription slip given by the dentist. Dental Aide checks the prescription slip given by the dentist and gives the prescribed medicine, if it is available. Step 4: Client Feedback. Dental aide gives the Client Satisfaction Measurement Survey via hard copy or Google Form. Patient signs the logbook after the dental care consultation and answers the Client Satisfaction Measurement Survey Form.

Nurse sends the HSSS QR Code thru email. Applicant answers the Health Services Satisfaction Survey (HSSS) posted or emailed to them. chunks.section_title: Procedure for Issuance of Admission Slip
chunks.process_name: Procedure for Issuance of Admission Slip
chunks.content: Step 1: Presentation of the Requirements Needed. Student presents the signed excuse letter and the photocopy of their parent/guardian’s ID at the Guidance and Counselling Office. The Guidance Office Staff checks the requirements submitted by the student. Step 2: Accomplishment of Admission Slip Form. The student fills out the 2 copies of Admission Slip Form. The guidance office staff reviews and signs the filled-out Admission Slip Form. Step 3: Review and Approval of the Subject Teacher. The student submits the accomplished Admission Slip Forms with attachments to respective subject teacher for signature. The subject teacher signs the Admission Slip. Step 4: Submission of Accomplished Admission Slip Form. Student returns to the Guidance and Counseling Office and submits the signed admission slip alongside with the signed excuse letter of parent/guardian and the photocopy of the parent/guardian’s ID. The guidance staff checks the signed admission slip together with the attachments and gives the student the student’s copy of the admission slip.  Contacts: Email: tupt.guidance@tup.edu.ph, Facebook: TUP TAGUIG Guidance Office, Teams: tupt.guidance@tup.edu.ph

chunks.section_title: Procedure on Request for Replacement of Lost / Damaged ID
chunks.process_name: Procedure on Request for Replacement of Lost / Damaged ID
chunks.content: Step 1: Submission of Document Requirements for Loss or Damaged ID. The student secures and submits an affidavit of loss for loss ID. For damaged ID, student presents the damaged ID to the OSA Staff. The OSA staff checks the documents submitted. Step 2: Filling-Out of Application Form for Student ID (FM-OSA-015). The OSA Staff issues the FM-OSA-015 form. The student fills out the FM-OSA-015 and submits to the OSA staff once done filling out. The OSA Staff checks the completeness of the FM-OSA-015 form submitted by the student and advises the student to pay the amount of ₱150.00 to the Cashier’s Office. Step 3: Payment of Fees. The student pays the amount of ₱150.00 at the Cashier’s Office. The Cashier’s staff issues receipt upon receiving the payment. Step 4: Submission of Documents and Printing of New ID. The student proceeds to the library after paying and presents the following documents: receipt, notarized affidavit of loss for loss ID or damaged ID for damaged ID, Certificate of Registration, and Application for New ID (FM-OSA-015) to the Librarian. The librarian accepts and collects the documents submitted, encodes any changes in the ID information, reprints the ID of the student, and issues the new ID printed to the student. The student signs the log sheet upon receiving the newly printed ID and proceeds to the OSA for the validation sticker.

chunks.section_title: Procedure on Request for Temporary ID Gate Pass
chunks.process_name: Procedure on Request for Temporary ID Gate Pass
chunks.content: The Temporary ID Gate Pass Form (FM-OSA-011) is issued when a student lost their ID or it was damaged, and the issuance of their new ID is pending or is on process. To use the Temporary ID Gate Pass, students must present the signed FM-OSA-011 to the security personnel upon entering the University premises. Step 1: Verification. The student presents Certificate of Registration (COR) proof of enrollment for the current term to the OSA Staff. The OSA staff verifies the COR presented and issues the Temporary ID Gate Pass Form (FM-OSA-011). Step 2: Filling-Out Form. The student fills out the temporary gate pass blank form (FM-OSA-011) and submits to the OSA staff once done filling out. The OSA Staff verifies and signs the FM-OSA-011. Step 3: Temporary ID Gate Pass Validity. OSA staff sets the date of the temporary gate pass validity and releases the form to the student.  Contacts: Email: tupt.osa@tup.edu.ph, Facebook: TUP-Taguig Office of the Student Affairs, Teams: tupt.osa@tup.edu.ph

chunks.section_title: Emergency Response Guide
chunks.content: Fire Emergency (Action: Evacuate): Drop down to the floor and crawl low, under any smoke to your exit. Heavy smoke and poisonous gases collect first along the ceiling. If you cannot get to someone needing assistance, leave the home and call 9-1-1 or the fire department. Tell the emergency operator where the person is located. If you open a door, open it slowly. Be ready to shut it quickly if heavy smoke or fire is present. If you cannot get out, close the door and cover vents and cracks around doors with cloth or tape to keep smoke out. Earthquake Emergency (Action: Duck, Cover and Hold): Wherever you are, drop down to your hands and knees and hold on to something sturdy. If you are using a wheelchair or walker with a seat, make sure your wheels are locked and remain seated until the shaking stops. Cover your head and neck with your arms. If a sturdy table or desk is nearby, crawl underneath it for shelter. If no shelter is nearby, crawl next to an interior wall away from windows. If you are under a table or desk, hold on with one hand and be ready to move with it if it moves. Eruption Emergency (Action: Move to a Safe Location): Listen to the radio and news for civil defense advice and follow instructions. If outside at the time of eruption, seek shelter in a car or a building. If caught in volcanic ashfalls, wear a dust mask or use a handkerchief or cloth over your nose and mouth. Stay indoors as volcanic ash is a health hazard, especially if you have respiratory difficulties such as asthma or bronchitis. Emergency Emergency (Action: Contact Front Desk): Follow your emergency plan. Get your emergency kit. Make sure you are safe before assisting others. Listen to the radio or television for information from local officials and follow their instructions. Stay put until all is safe or until you are ordered to evacuate. Emergency Numbers: Bureau of Fire Protection: (02) 8426-0219, (02) 8426-0246, Philippine Red Cross: 143 or (02) 8527-8385 loc 185, Philippine National Police: 117 or (02) 8722-0650, MMDA: (02) 8824-6110 to 77
chunks.answer: For Emergency Response Guide, follow the emergency instructions. For example, in case of Fire, Evacuate.
chunks.citation: Campus Safety and Emergency Response, Emergency Response Guide
steps: Fire: Evacuate. Drop down to the floor and crawl low, under any smoke to your exit.
Earthquake: Duck, Cover and Hold. Wherever you are, drop down to your hands and knees and hold on to something sturdy.
Eruption: Move to a Safe Location. Listen to the radio and news for civil defense advice and follow instructions.
Emergency: Contact Front Desk. Follow your emergency plan.

chunks.content: Onsite: The client can answer the feedback form available in the lobby of the Admin Building. Drop it in the feedback and complaints box or submit it to the Public Assistance & Complaints Desk Officer. Online: The Survey link form can be accessed via TUPT CSM through this link: https://forms.gle/ymFkxFqN1ddpdkx5 The client may send an email to tupt.customerfeedback@tup.edu.ph. Other concern may also be emailed to the Quality Assurance Office at tupt.qataguig@tup.edu.ph. Client may call (632) 8247-5250 to 54 loc. 135.

chunks.section_title: How Feedback is Processed
chunks.content: Onsite: The Desk Officer receives and records all feedback submitted. Feedback needing answers are immediately forwarded to the relevant office or process owner. The concerned office is required to answer within the day or at least three (3) days from the receipt of such feedback. Online: The Receiving Officer validates the feedback and verifies its nature. The feedback is endorsed to the Head of the concerned office. Upon receipt of the reply from the concerned office, the client shall be informed via email or phone call, if contact numbers are provided by the client.

chunks.section_title: How to File Complaint
chunks.content: Onsite: The client can fill out the complaint form found in the lobby of the Admin Building and submit it to the Complaints Desk Officer. Online: Complaints can be coursed via TUPT CSM through this link: https://forms.gle/ymFkxFqN1ddpdkx5 Complaints can also be coursed through emails: tupt.customerfeedback@tup.edu.ph and tupt.qataguig@tup.edu.ph. The complainant must provide name and contact information, details of the complaint, and name of person/office being complained. Complaints may also be coursed through phone calls at 8247-5250 loc. 135.

chunks.section_title: How Complaint is Processed
chunks.content: The Customer Feedback Officer validates all complaints received on a daily basis and forwards them to the Head of the relevant section or office. The concerned Section Head addresses the complaints and investigates, if necessary. After the concern has been addressed, the Section Head shall submit an incident report or deficiency report to the Division Head/Assistant Director, for appropriate action. The Section Head shall give the feedback to the client through email. The client may also follow up through email or phone call at (632) 8247-5250 to 54 loc. 135.

chunks.section_title: Austerity Measures in the Campus - Electricity and Water
chunks.content: Reference: Office Order No. 7 s. 2025. ACUs and other electrical office equipment should be energized from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM only, except during the conduct of night classes and overtime services of non-teaching staff where they can be used up to 7:00 PM only. Airconditioning units must be maintained at low cool during lunch breaks (12:00-1:00). Digital aircons should set the unit at F2 (24). Electric fans, lights, ACUs and other similar loads should be shut off after classes and office hours. Use of TV sets, if there are any, are allowed only for viewing of news and for special broadcasts, e.g. Malacañang announcement, SONA, etc. Ovens and other cooking appliances should only be used to support classroom laboratory activities. Computers not in use are to be turned off. Playing computer games and social networking is strictly prohibited in all classrooms and offices. The use of floodlights in the campus grounds is allowed only for PE and other related classes or curricular/major activities approved by proper authorities. Access to offices, workshops, or laboratory rooms during Sundays, Holidays, and other days when there are no classes is not allowed, unless prior permission is sought from proper authorities. Staying overnight in the campus is not allowed unless authorized by concerned university officials. All leaking faucets and toilet flushes should be reported immediately and acted upon by the Maintenance Staff. Wasteful use of water must be discouraged. Official vehicle trips should be reduced through trip planning and passenger pooling to save on gasoline expenses. Use of electricity at the TUP Gymnasium will be limited to 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM with prior permission sought from proper authorities. I.T. Building Auditorium shall be used for official function only.

chunks.section_title: Austerity Measures in the Campus - Supplies and Materials
chunks.content: Reference: Office Order No. 7 s. 2025. All supplies and materials are strictly for office use only. Corresponding penalty for unauthorized use or bringing out of such shall be meted out to erring employees. Bond papers and other paper products should be recycled for internal communication and reports. Use of refill ink / continuous ink supply system should be used instead of original ink cartridges for computer printers. Promotion of paperless transactions and communications through the use of electronic transmission.

chunks.section_title: Austerity Measures in the Campus - Communication
chunks.content: Reference: Office Order No. 7 s. 2025. All telephone lines are strictly for official use. Personal calls must be regulated. Instead of using office telephones, the personnel may use their own mobile phone for official transactions that need immediate response. Use of internet/e-mail in communication instead of courier services, unless otherwise required, should be encouraged. Requests for F137/Transcript of Records of new students are to be hand-carried instead of using postage stamps.

chunks.section_title: Austerity Measures in the Campus - Repair and Maintenance
chunks.content: Reference: Office Order No. 7 s. 2025. Recycling of scrap steel/wood and galvanized iron roofing should be utilized for minor repair and maintenance. Utilization of existing surplus materials for repair instead of purchasing new materials. Proper use and maintenance of office equipment and facilities must be observed to minimize maintenance costs and prolong their useful life.
